STEP 2 - Vessel size:

b) Reference: the Brussels sprouts are roughly 3-4 cm across. Across the plate's width I can fit roughly 6-7 sprouts laid side by side, giving about 22-26 cm. Trusting both cues, width ≈ 24 cm.
Area = 24 x 24 = 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items (countable, Brussels sprouts, cooked, roasted/charred):

- Hidden under others: the pile is only one layer deep, so add ~1 more. Total ≈ 14 sprouts.
- Each sprout is about 15-20 g; using 18 g each: 14 x 18 = 252 g.
- Footprint check: the sprouts cover roughly 12% of the plate, about 69 cm². With an average thickness of about 3 cm (one sprout diameter, stacked up to ~2 at the thickest), volume ≈ 69 x 2.5 ≈ 170 ml; at cooked-vegetable density 0.6 g/ml gives ≈ 100 g. The per-piece count gives a higher value, so I take the midpoint: about 180 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible on the plate; the surface is bare white. No extra items.

STEP 5 - Energy: cooked Brussels sprouts with a little oil, roughly 40-50 kcal per 100 g. Use 45 kcal/100 g.

Total weight ≈ 180 g; energy ≈ 180 x 0.45 ≈ 81 kcal.
